setting.note: A brother and sister grow up at a riverside mill in the fictional town of St Ogg's, drawn from Gainsborough on the tidal River Trent in Lincolnshire; loyalty, thwarted love and family ruin play out along the water until a great flood carries the story to its end.

rights.originalWork: First published 1860. George Eliot (Mary Ann Evans) died in 1880; the work is in the public domain. Mapped as a cited work: no text stored, no passages reproduced. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of the text, in any territory.
rights.attribution: The Mill on the Floss, George Eliot (1860). Locations mapped by Read the Places; not affiliated with or endorsed by any estate or publisher.

palette.note: The green-brown of a working river, weed and mill-water and flood, the element that runs through the whole book. A cited book's colour is not a quotation; it still has to be legible, and this clears WCAG AA on paper.
